attrs.description: The client portal and operator app.
Storybook for the portal's pages and shell: the real app on a fake server (MSW, `web/src/mocks/`)
The portal Storybook's preview: `@wren/ui`'s frame over the app's stylesheet, and a fake server (MSW) started before each story
The portal's page stories as tests (`@wren/ui/storybook/tests`)
The axe color-contrast scan: every portal page, in every look, all text at 4.5:1 with no large-text exception

What the portal's browser e2e scripts share (writes-e2e.ts, outreach-e2e.ts): the local preview's address, Chrome, a fake Restate for the handlers the preview can't run, the tab hidden and back, a fresh page, and the runner
The portal's libraries in a real browser: the address on TanStack Router, the lists on TanStack Table and Virtual, the forms on React Hook Form

Engage (was Outreach) in a real browser: its tabs in the nav and gone from Content's, old Marketing and Outreach addresses landing on the new ones, Invites' To approve and To message, the Account filter, and two writes through the one write path: an invite approved by a double press goes once, and a comment on someone's post sent with the tab hidden goes once and lands on return
The portal on your machine, against your local databases: the built app plus the same API, called in-process instead of through Restate and sign-in

The portal's screens as JSON, for kestrel's ui layer (kestrel.json `layers.ui.dump`): areas in order, each app (and the name it is exported as) and its pages, each page's template and record or its own file

Comment threads in a real browser, on Marketing → Comments since Engage went outbound only (2026-10-16-outreach-app.md), on a local preview seeded by `packages/content/test/threads-preview.ts`: one person's two comments show as one row, newest first; the row's whole thread draws nested; Reply from Wren on a deep reply sends that comment's ref, once however often it's pressed; and on a phone the thread opens as its own sheet
The one write path in a real browser: a send, a draft then a send, and a set-aside with undo, each with the tab hidden mid-write, a row switch or a reload, must end with the page matching the server
The few parts of `ws` the preview uses (no @types/ws in the repo)
`/api/agent`: Wren for AI tools, by a CLI and a skill
A client's public booking page, no sign-in:  - On the client's own host: `/book`, `/book/<tag>`, `/booking/<token>`, and its API at `/__book/<handler>`
Which build of the app a tab runs (wa-ovo)
The portal on this Mac against prod: `pnpm dev` runs this Worker in Vite (`@cloudflare/vite-plugin`) and reads prod through Restate
Dictation's server adapter: `/api/dictate`
The signing page's paths, no sign-in:  - `GET /o/d/<token>`: the document, rendered by `Documents/serve`
The Worker's small shared parts: JSON answers and calls to Restate's ingress
The Worker's bindings
The portal on a client's own host
A pasted key's way in: `POST /api/keys/stage` here, then the sign-in Lambda, which seals it and answers a ref
One cap per visitor on every path anyone may post to without signing in: Sites forms and the tracker, site chat, document signing, booking and AI tools
Live notes: `/api/notes/live/<id>` opens a WebSocket to that note's room, one Durable Object per note (`NoteRoom`), which runs `@wren/notes/room`
Learn's pictures and audio through the app's own origin, so the page's CSP stays at 'self' for images and media, however many hosts thumbnails and podcasts live on
`/oauth/<kind>/<name>`: where a provider sends a person back after connecting something
Stripe's webhook for pay links: `POST /__pay/stripe/<client>` on the app host
`POST /api/pulse`: the app's reads that fall due together (the sidebar's counts, the bell, a badge) as one request
The portal's services: the first path part after /api/, the Restate service behind it, and each route's need (`@wren/core/access`), which that service's guard checks
Sites' public paths, no sign-in:  - `/o/<slug>`: a live data page, Wren's on the apex, a client's on its own host
Turnstile's check at the edge: the booking page and every Sites form submit
Sends told live: one `WriteWatch` Durable Object per signed-in person and site
The client portal (R14) and the public demo (R15), one Worker on two hosts
A write's state, read from Restate's own record of it
The portal: who's signed in, whose workspace, and Wren's apps for it
This login's access in one workspace, as `delivery/me` sent it: the same `Who` the server's guard reads, so the web's `canAt` and the server's `can` answer alike
The portal API: POST /api/<service>/<route> with JSON (`delivery/home`, `reactivation/recordsList`)
The apps this viewer may open in the workspace on screen: what `App` shows, handed to a page that lists them (Admin → Systems)
The sidebar leads with five fixed items: the Map, then Inbox, People, Money and Admin (SIDEBAR)
What a portal command meant, for autotrack (the recorder in wren_automation/autotrack)
Where a booking page is: its API base (`/c/<client>` on the app host, nothing on the client's own host), and whether it books (`/book/<tag>`) or shows one call (`/booking/<token>`)
A client's public booking page (`book.html`), served by the portal Worker (`src/book.ts`) on the client's own host or at `/c/<client>` on the app host
A page that throws breaks itself, never the shell around it
`pnpm dev` only: a mark that this tab reads prod, and whether it may write
The portal's dictation: routes each press to the browser's model, our server or the browser's own speech, runs the mic through `startDictation`, and hands the kit's `Dictate` its words
The page's one dictation engine (engine.ts); null where there's no browser
Model files from the network, kept in Cache Storage: onnxruntime's wasm (gzipped, from our own origin) for dictation and reading aloud, and reading's voices
The mic for dictation: 16 kHz mono slices and their loudness, until closed
The browser adapter's `Transcriber`: the speech model in its worker (model.worker.ts), loaded on the first mic press
The browser's speech model, off the page's thread: Moonshine base on WebGPU through transformers.js
What the page and the speech model's worker say to each other
The server adapter's `Transcriber`: each segment as a WAV to the portal Worker's `/api/dictate` (apps/portal/src/dictate.ts), which asks our speech server
The fallback adapter: the browser's own speech recognition as `Ears`
A post's own player address from its link: YouTube's id, and the embeds the CSP lets in (`public/_headers` frame-src)
⌘K's record search: an app's `find` over the record type one of its list pages shows
Feature flags for this login here, as `delivery/me` evaluated them (`@wren/core/flags`)
The column of a board of cards (Notes → Board, Journeys → Board): a drop target with its name and count, the cards, and a line when empty
A pasted key goes to `/api/keys/stage` alone: it comes back as a ref and its last 4
One record's calls run in the order made: words saved as a box lost focus land before the Approve that took it
Loading a portal call into a component: a TanStack Query read (`@wren/ui` data layer)
What a viewer keeps in this browser (a remembered pick), never needed: a blocked store reads as nothing
His own look over Wren's workspace (Settings → Look), read by the frame and its settings page
The versions that touched one node or one line, newest first, as a section of a card (the node's details, its edit card, a line's edit card)
The banner over the Map while a draft is open (`?draft=<id>`): its name, the version it started from, who made it, its state, and (when live moved on) the newest version
The History card's Drafts tab: the shape's drafts, one row each (name, state, the version it started from, who, when)
A focus page: one part of the Map at `/map/<kind>/<id>`, a set at `/map/parts/<parts>`, a saved view at `/map/view/<id>`
The Map's History, a card over the canvas, in two tabs
"/" for Wren's team: the Map of the workspace's shape, and Today under it (artifact section 07)
Importing a shape file onto the Map: the file is read by the server (`shapePreview`, which saves nothing)
The Map: the shape of the workspace drawn as a metro map by `MetroMap`, edge to edge, in the app's own theme
The Map's details for one part (a pick), a card over the canvas
A server refusal as the server says it: one line, or a list when the reason has many lines
Names a version: a short form under it (name, and a note if it helps)
Today's tasks (artifact section 07): one card per person track, late first
Undo one line of a difference: the line of "Version a to b" that says what one change did
The Map's drafts and history lines, pure (no reads, so a test imports it alone): the address of an opened draft, what each draft state allows, and the words of a blame line
A file for the person: a text downloaded, and the text of a file they picked
A focus page's model: what `/map/<kind>/<id>`, `/map/parts/<parts>` and `/map/view/<id>` name, read from the metro body
What one viewer keeps of the Map in this browser: the fold depth, the folds opened by hand and the open panel
The Map's data, pure (no reads, so a test imports it alone): the windows, what a read gives, and the lines a panel says
Where the Map's panels sit: over the canvas, never beside it, so the graph keeps its whole width
The Map's reads: the newest shape with its versions, the window's numbers per station, track and line, the open journeys, and the ghosts (a journey on a node the newest version dropped)
Where a Map node opens: the app that manages it, one table
The live shape, read light (the shape alone, no numbers): the graph nodes for Admin → Systems (an app is found by a node's `via` and `channel`) and the metro stations for ⌘K
Today's tasks, pure
The Map's drawing as plain data, pure: the stored metro body plus the window's numbers and the open journeys, as the `MetroView` that `MetroMap` draws
Saved views of the Map: a named set of parts kept in the workspace's `saved_views` under record `map`, its params `parts=<parts>`
The portal's server, faked in the browser for page stories
Account pages' reads and writes for stories (`../../modules/account/`): webhooks, AI tools, People, Connectors, Social, Mail, and a person's access
Each app's own first read, past the records pages: the reactivation run, the delivery home, learn's shelves, notes, the calendar, deals' board
The workflow Canvas's answers: one small workflow (`wren`: leads in, a first touch, a follow-up, replies out) and the editor's writes (save, publish, ask Claude, a dry test)
The fake server's answers, path → body (`../api.ts`), for every page story
The Journeys board's reads and writes (`../../modules/deals/board.tsx`): one synthetic shape
Rows with long words, for the stories that hold a list's widths: names, roles and firms as long as real ones run, beside short figures

The Map's drafts, blame, tags and undo on the fake server: synthetic drafts of the sample shape (`pipeline.shape_draft`, a record the worker adds with the server half; until then the fake serves it here), and answers for every route the History and the panels call
`pipeline/mapRead` from a story's record answers: the shape's detail, the window's number rows and the open journeys, as the server's `mapAnswerOf` gives them
The Map's reads beyond the shared ones (`journeys.ts`, `offers.ts`): the answers of the D1 contract (`@wren/pipeline/history`)
Wren's marketing, for Today and Marketing: pieces and their branches, and the week's cadence
Who is signed in, for page stories: a client's owner with every app, or Wren's admin
What waits on Wren's team (`../../moves.ts`), one record each: a call within a day, approvals, inbox items, replies, access asks
The Offers and Numbers pages' reads (`../../modules/offers`, `../../modules/numbers`, the pipelines tabs) and the books pages that moved to Numbers

Every records page's reads (`<product>/recordsTypes`, `recordsList`, `recordsGet`, `recordsCounts`), answered with the server's own types: the meta of every record type the worker serves (`virtual:record-types`, made in `.storybook/main.ts` from `apps/worker/src/record-types.ts`)
A made-up birdwatch run as `weaver serve` sends it: Research's story and tree test read it
What the shell reads on every page: the account, its bells and badges
Studio's fakes: the drafts that wait (ContentDesk.waiting) and a shape with two offer lines
Sample data for the Wren pages that draw lists with `Rows`: Ask, made workflows, the home's client health, automations, the dossier, a split's ended arms
A page story: the whole portal at one address, on the fake server (`./api.ts`)
Every record type's meta the worker serves: `.storybook/main.ts` makes it in Node
An app in the portal: a row in the sidebar under its area, its pages as tabs at /<app>/<page>
One person's access, as sentences: their role's grants, then their extra grants with End now, Add, and the ended ones under History
Access's pages and actions: roles, grants, issues and asks, the same for Wren's team (Team and Inbox) and a client's people (Account)
Accounts: each account the client has with Wren, what its setup has done and what's left
AI tools: a person's access tokens for the `wren` CLI and its skill, which Claude Code and other agents run
Account → Connectors: the client's HubSpot, QuickBooks and Jobber, one framed section each with its state (Needs setup, Not connected, Connected, Broken), what it reads and what it tells workflows
Domain: this portal on the client's own address, like portal.theirfirm.com
Settings → Fields and Business facts
Billing's one quiet line: the live tools the client has installed that we built in place of a SaaS, and what they'd cost a month bought separately (`@wren/core/in-house`)
Daily limits: each research bucket and daily count, what holds now and where it comes from
A workspace's look: Account's Look page for its owners, a client's record for Wren's team
Account → Mail: the client's mailboxes, each with its state, what blocks it and the next step; above them, each domain's one admin step as a checklist with the links and the ID to paste
Now: the setup items waiting on whoever looks
The account at a glance: who the company is to us, what they bought, who's on it, what's owed

Account → Social in Wren's own workspace, for the team: each channel Wren posts to, with its account, how it posts, its token, its last post and last failure, and a Check that asks autobrowse whether the account still answers
People: who sees this account's projects
Get set up: Today's card over the owner's setups
Account → Social: the client's own social accounts, one framed section per platform with its state (Not connected, Waiting on review, Connected, Broken), what blocks it and the next step
Vendors: each vendor a client's parts read through, on Wren's key (managed) or its own, today's room and the month's use
Webhooks: the client's own URLs that hear events as they happen, each signed
Your settings: the mail this person gets from us (D9), dictation on this device, and how they sign in
Account → Billing: an invoice's detail says how to pay it by bank transfer, each value with its copy button, and offers its PDF
Your settings, Dictation: which way this device turns speech into text, the browser's own speech as a fallback (off by default), and why the mic is missing when it is
The client's account, reached from their name at top left: the company, its people, each person's own settings, billing
The account's calls, one key each: a write re-reads its call (`retry`), never a new key
Your settings, Reading aloud: on or off on this device, the voice, the speed, and a sample
How Accounts and Vendors say things: a setup run's state and steps, a vendor's mode
Account → Social's pieces for one connected account: its picture, and a connected TikTok's numbers (followers, likes, videos, its newest videos with their views), read as the page opened
Accounts and vendors from Wren's side: a client's in short on its Clients record, and this month's managed usage across clients
Analytics: how people find and use the site
What can be done to a call: the Calls list and the Schedule's side panel share them
The Calendar page's date maths, on the viewer's own clock: which days a view shows, the range it asks for, where a block sits in its day, and side-by-side lanes for calls that overlap
Calendar: calls booked on our own calendar
Calls recorded on William's Mac
The Schedule: a calendar's calls the way a calendar shows them, on the viewer's own clock: Wren's in Wren's workspace, the client's own in a client's (its database, through `calendar/*`)
How a booked call went: Won, Not yet, No-show, Not a fit
A booked call's page: the header says who, the company and when, with the outcome buttons; under it the three lines worth reading first, and how it went once it's marked
Calls: a client's booked calls, each with its pre-call brief and how it went
Journeys → Board: one board for the shape, a column per node that holds people (every node but a source), by depth then name, a card per open journey
A journey's fit to the offer's ICP (`packages/pipeline/src/icp.ts`), on its detail: the score as a fact, the reasons and the checks with nothing to go on as a section
The id of Wren's pipelines app (`deals` until 2026-10-19)
Journeys: each person's way through the shape
The tabs Wren's own pipelines app adds to the shared Journeys pages: the deals, the calls and the entries
Documents → Documents and Templates: contracts, proposals and estimates written here, from a template or blank, sent by email or text to be signed
Documents: contracts, proposals and estimates from the client's templates, sent by text or email, signed on a page under its name, a deposit on signing
The Inbox's queues: one list, read by Overview E (what waits, ranked by the oldest wait) and by each queue's own page (`late`: the same date field and promise)
The portal's apps, in this order within each sidebar area (areas.ts): a client's work first, then each product, the Marketplace, then Wren's own (Wren's workspace only)
Learn's calls and shapes, as LearnConsole answers them (packages/learn/src/drive.ts)
The portal's bell, in the top bar of every workspace with Learn: what rang for you lately, new ones counted on it
Learn's Items: a place from the sidebar (Inbox, Watch later, a collection, a source), as a feed of cards, a list or a compact list (remembered per viewer)
Find someone to follow by name or topic, on YouTube, Reddit, LinkedIn, X, Instagram and TikTok at once (`ReachDesk.findCreators`): no address needed
Learn's places and collections, as tabs in the portal's sidebar like every app's pages: Items (Inbox, Watch later, Starred, Saved by you, All items, Archived), the collections tree, then tags
Learn's home: what you were watching, this week's best, then new from your sources, one shelf per type, and the SOPs items went into lately

Learn: what a workspace saves from a phone or the portal and what the sources it follows publish, read, scored against its SOPs, and kept like a drive: a home of shelves, items as cards, a list or a compact list, collections that nest, tags, a Watch later queue, and each item played or read in place

One item, in place: a YouTube video plays here (youtube-nocookie, driven by postMessage, so no outside script loads) with its key moments above and its transcript beside, each line a seek; an episode plays through `/media`; an Instagram, TikTok or X post shows its own embed; an article reads clean
What Learn draws for a type: its name, its mark, its length, and a picture through the app's own `/media` (apps/portal/src/media.ts), so the CSP stays at 'self' for every thumbnail host
Learn's Save a link box, search across every transcript, and the phone's share target (/learn/add?url=)
Learn's dialogs and menus: move to a collection, tag, add to an SOP, name a collection, the keys
Learn's Sources, grouped by kind: follow a channel, podcast, newsletter or blog by its page or feed, say how loud each is, stop one
Learn's Today: your daily digest
The Library's Workflows: each one's steps, and a link onto the Workflows canvas, or for one saved as a template, to the Marketplace page that installs it, and Delete for Wren's team
The Library: the words Wren sends and the sequences that send them (Wren's workspace)
The Library's Media: the file itself, played or shown, signed for a while
A template's numbers in the Library: each version's sends, replies and bookings, each variant point's options by reply rate, and the campaigns that sent it (`templates.template` detail)
Library → Sections: every block a Sections page is built from, with its blurb, its fields and a preview drawn from its sample words
A sequence as the graph kit draws it, and the words its numbers read as: leads in, then each step with its template, what it sent, its reply rate and its variants, the wait on the wire before it
A sequence's page in the Library: its steps drawn on the graph kit (the canvas the workflow editor draws on, read-only here), then a row per step with its template, live version, variants and numbers
The Library's Snippets: saved replies and blocks, edited in place (the record's `edits`), with a star that makes one a favorite: favorites come first in every Insert picker
Library, Templates: every template in its folder (the kit's `Browser`), and the open one's editor with a live preview for the made-up lead, its history with a diff and restore, and its numbers

A post's numbers on its page: how it did, with a sparkline a metric and its state where it isn't read; the retention curve; where viewers came from; its title, thumbnail and hook windows; what it brought to the site; its conversation
To approve: templates, workflows, pages and retires asked to go live, replies waiting on a yes, the combined action list, and each page's draft box

Drafts finished in place: each page declares where its rows hold a draft and what sends it, and the detail draws it as `@wren/ui`'s draft box: typed and saved there, Ask Claude under it, the turns above, Undo beside the newest change
Marketing → Auto-reply: per channel, what happens when someone writes in
Write's Blog box: a post for wrenautomation.com/blog in Markdown
Write's Carousel box: slides typed as one block (a blank line between slides), a caption, and where it goes: Instagram's swipe, LinkedIn's document post
Booking clicks by first touch, a bar a week for 8 weeks: the Overview's one chart
Comment row actions, a comment's thread view, and activity

One conversation per Inbox thread: everything with the person on every channel, oldest at the top; a reply box that sends on the channel picked, or asks for a yes; and a note box for the team, never sent
A Wren service's handler through the console (`console/call`), as Studio's boxes call it
DM row actions: reply, read and drop one of ours not sent yet
DMs as the person meets them on a laptop and a phone: a thread's replies, and William's copy
Outreach → Engage: which model writes reach drafts, and how each one's drafts fared
A post's fields and slides saves patch their page from the answer (ContentDesk `fields` and `slides` answer `saved`, the parts of the shape they moved): no read of the draft again after a save
A post's row actions: drafts (approve, reject, edit, pass), promos, swaps and sends that may have gone out; ads and texts
Outreach → Engage: its draft boxes and actions, and Feed's Explore
Marketing → Experiments (`marketing.experiment`): a site flag with a goal
Marketing → Facts: what every draft may claim about William and Wren (`@wren/core/facts`), one fact a row
Marketing → Feed

A post's fields past its words: its funnel first, then the form drawn from the platform's shape in three groups (Basics, Media, Details), each field saved on its own, and the post as its platform shows it beside them, live as he types
Captions and text drawn over the video as the render draws them, shared with the storyboard's frames
The Finish view's data: the edit and record types, its constants, and the pure sums over them (times, stable JSON, what a format shows, what a version changed)
The Finish view's hooks and pointer helpers: a steady signed URL, a drag, a measured width
The Finish panels: Text, Captions, Cover and Shapes, and the Short crops picker
The Shorts and the layout in the finishing view: what `wren video set shorts`, `layout` and `camBox` change, as rows he edits and saves
The Finish stage: the player over the recording with the view switch and the bar under it
The Finish timeline: filmstrip, in and out, cut edges, text bars, caption lines, cover, playhead

Finishing a video: the player over the recording's playback copy, skipping what's cut; text and captions drawn live over it; each shape's crop dragged in place; the timeline under it with the filmstrip, in and out, cut edges, text bars, caption lines, the cover and the playhead
A post's place in the funnel: its stage, where it points and the link it carries
A lander page's heatmap, drawn on its newest replay in the `/replay` frame (`../../replay.ts`)
The Inbox's row actions: typed ids, waiting states, the thread's assign, close and snooze
Marketing's pages: content, ads, search, texts and site visits as one funnel
The Module objects: Wren's Ads and Content apps, and a client's Marketing
The pages: Inbox, Done and To approve, Content's day, reviews, ad days, the site's pages, and `MARKETING_PAGES`, the one list the team apps take from
Marketing → Pieces' built-in views: one press sets what, state and order together, so the usual looks (what waits on him, what is scheduled, the carousels) are a click, not three
Pieces: each thing William made, once, with where it went under it
Reads on his click (audience, discovery), comment keywords, and the places discovery found
Marketing → Today: what to make, by what he makes, not by platform
A post as its feed shows it on a laptop and a phone, from the record's detail
A sent comment's proof on its Engage page: Live, Hidden, Missing or Checking
Marketing → Reports: the Overview's numbers mailed to members every Monday or 1st at 9:00
What Write's Carousel and Story boxes share once the content is in: where it goes, the three ways to send it, and what ContentDesk said back
A recorded lander view, played in the `/replay` frame (`../../replay.ts`) from signed chunk URLs
A post as its platform shows it, live as he types: YouTube's home, search and watch page, a Short, a Reel, TikTok, a Reddit post, LinkedIn's feed and an X post
A draft's editor shows the same idea's other platforms (`siblings` on the draft's detail), so every version of one piece is a click apart
A carousel's slides: edited in the draft, a strip of each slide as it renders, and the drawn files to download
Accounts (operator API keys), invites and connects: the social logins' row actions
One of our pieces beside its SOP: each standard number with ours, each closed set with ours, the patterns he kept or dropped, his calls judged, and up to 3 changes
Write's Story box: a photo from the phone or laptop, or a clip he already cut, as a story on Instagram and the Facebook Page

A video's storyboard: the edit as frames, one per chapter (or run of sentences) and one per Short, each drawn as the Finish preview draws that moment: the picture, the corner camera, the captions, the text on it
What Studio's parts share: the kinds it makes, the platforms its words go to, the read of the drafts that wait, and the small words and times its rows say
Studio's compose view: one kind at a time, the kind tabs on top
Studio's head: what the plan still asks for this week, a card per piece, and the New row, a card per kind
Offer lines in Studio: the shape's lines (read once, kept on the device), a line's colour square and its name

Studio's waiting drafts, on the shared `Rows`: an idea a row (kind, words, line, platforms, slot, age), a check to approve it in place with an Undo, and a click that opens its platforms side by side to edit, rewrite, post now or drop
Marketing → Studio: where content gets made
Marketing → Surveys (`marketing.survey`): one question, with when and who as words on the row
William's texts as the person gets them on a phone and a laptop, filled with sample facts
A comment's whole conversation: the post, our comment and every reply under it, nested, each with its own Reply from Wren and a link to it on the site
An X thread in one draft: its posts edited one box each, counted as X counts them (the funnel link rides on the last), split, merged and moved; and the chain as X shows it
Thread row actions: a comment drafted on someone else's post, and a found thread's reply

A TikTok post's settings as TikTok's Direct Post rules ask (developers.tiktok.com/doc/ content-sharing-guidelines, `@wren/core/content/tiktok`): the account it posts to, who can see it with nothing picked for you, comments, duets and stitches off until turned on and greyed where the account turned them off, the content disclosure with its labels, the video against the account's longest, and TikTok's declaration above the yes
A draft's versions: each one with who wrote it and when, what was decided, and the kit's `Diff` between any two
A video edit's answer patches its page (`VideoDesk` set, line, cut, words and undo answer `view`, the edit as the page draws it): no read of the video again after a save
The Videos shelf's reads, kept apart from the page so they test without a browser

Studio's Videos: the newest recordings and rendered videos as cards (first frame, length, state, where each went), and the editor opened right there in Studio (`?video=<id>`), the Recordings page's own record body at full width
Video row actions: approve (upload to YouTube), privacy, promos and the rest of a recording's life

A video's detail (`marketing.video`), edited in place: the preview; the title, description, tags, chapters, Shorts titles and thumbnail text, each saved on blur; the cuts with the words they strike, Keep or Cut; a span of transcript words picked and cut; Ask Claude with Undo
Setup's one add-on (`Offer.addOn`): the component that fits what this client bought, checked already, with Install and Skip

A component's record, below its fields (what's missing is one): what it takes and gives, what runs inside it, how we expect it to generalize, where it's used, what it needs and provides, and what the viewer may do
A client's record: its Templates, each with where it stands, and its Components, what it has installed, each with its settings, prices left out
The Map: every component and what it builds on, left to right, drawn from the manifests' `requires` (the catalog's Needs), so it shows what actually runs
